title: Tenant role lifecycle and member onboarding playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a comprehensive UI/UX playbook that guides the design and interaction patterns for RBAC v2 role lifecycle and member onboarding in the Redwood Console. This ticket focuses on the role creation/edit flow, member assignment (individual and bulk), SSO/SAML group mapping visibility, audit-log hooks for role changes, and admin controls for temporary access and delegation. Aim is to reduce ambiguous permission assignments, make change history discoverable, and provide safe preview/simulation prior to applying role changes in production tenants.
acceptance_criteria: Role editor supports composing roles with statements (allow/deny) including resource scoping and conditions and displays a readable human summary before save
Member assignment panel supports single add, CSV bulk invite, and SSO/group mapping preview with clear resolution status (mapped / unmapped / conflict)
Permission preview modal shows effective permissions for a selected member and highlights newly granted/revoked permissions prior to save
All role create/update/delete events include an audit metadata payload (actor, timestamp, diff, reason) and mockup shows where console surfaces link to audit logs
Temporary roles (time-bound grants) are creatable with a clear expiration UI and automated renewal/notification path
Design includes error states for permission simulations that cannot be computed (e.g., external group query failure) and provides safe rollback hints
Design notes and annotated Figma screens are linked and have sign-off from PM and Security
Edge-case flows documented: large orgs (10k+ users), cross-tenant admins, external SSO provider mapping changes
design_notes: Prioritize readable, non-technical summaries for business users while keeping an advanced JSON editor for power users
Expose a compact breadcrumb for role inheritance and parent templates to reduce cognitive load when editing derived roles
Member assignment UI should show resolution state for each entry: local user, SCIM user, SAML group -> mapped role, conflict with existing role, pending invite
When SSO group mappings change, surface a changelog entry with the computed delta and a one-click 'preview impact' that highlights affected members
Include a lightweight permission simulator: select member or role and test an action (e.g., cancel-dedicated-instance) to see allow/deny and reason
Make audit links contextual (e.g., next to Save button show 'View last 10 role changes for this tenant')
Design layout optimized for desktop; mobile should allow read-only inspection and member lookup but defer heavy edits to desktop
decisions: Show human-readable summary before saving roles (decision: keep both compact summary + optional raw JSON rule editor)
Combine bulk CSV + SCIM invite into a single 'Add members' flow to avoid fragmentation
Permission simulator will run against a cached index for responsiveness; fallback to async exact evaluation if cache miss
Temporary grants expire automatically; admin receives a notification and can choose to extend or let expire
Expose a 'safe mode' toggle for orgs that will require a two-step apply for role changes with audit comment required
tradeoffs: Simplicity vs power: showing simplified permissions reduces cognitive load for non-technical admins but may hide important conditional logic
Performance vs accuracy of simulator: cached simulation is fast but may be stale during rapid SSO group updates
Scope of UI: building too many admin workflows into the Console increases surface area; defer complex bulk reconciliation to a later admin tools project
Audit noise: surfacing granular change diffs increases transparency but may overwhelm incident response teams; include optional aggregation filters
